label: Arbora ecosystem
desc: People and agents enter through Arbora. Arbora admits each request. Agent Utilities runs the harness. Epistemic Graph stores and reasons. Source systems connect through the SDK.

children.label: People
children.desc: People use the system to ask questions and to run work. They send requests through a front end or a chat channel. They receive answers that cite their evidence.

children.label: MCP / REST / A2A clients
children.desc: External agents and applications call the system by protocol. They send MCP, REST or A2A calls to Arbora and receive typed results. Arbora admits each call before any effect occurs.

children.label: Arbora web UI
children.desc: The web UI shows the graph, the runs and the decisions in a browser. It sends typed operations to Arbora and receives projections back. It holds no data of its own.

children.label: Arbora API consumer
children.desc: A generated client calls typed Arbora operations. Effects keep the preview, confirm and step-up flow.

children.label: Generated client
children.desc: The client is generated from a pinned Arbora schema.

children.label: Route census
children.desc: A route census tracks domain routes that still need typed operations.

children.label: Typed domain operations
children.desc: Ontology, graph, atlas and object-set calls keep tenant semantics.

children.label: Auth and streaming
children.desc: Shared auth and streaming work without a service bearer. Each request carries its own correlation id.

children.label: Application surface
children.desc: The app surface declares each app route, capability and layout. Views follow the signed-in role.

children.label: AppSurface contract
children.desc: Each app declares its route, capability and layout states. An app cannot escalate privilege.

children.label: Brand layer
children.desc: The brand layer sets user-visible names. Package and runtime identifiers do not change.

children.label: Run harness and evolution views
children.desc: The run harness view is read-only. The evolution dashboard shows projections and evidence.

children.label: Goals, sessions and fleets
children.desc: One panel relates goals, sessions and fleets.

children.label: Graph and memory views
children.desc: Graph edits go through the engine. Refusals show in the view. Memory shows as synced files.

children.label: Large-data charts
children.desc: Charts bin large data and support selection.

children.label: Meetings and bookmarks
children.desc: Live meeting transcripts, summaries and bookmark search appear here.

children.label: Design flow and editor extensions
children.desc: Design artifacts run in a sandbox. Remote editor extensions stay compatible.

children.label: Browser design system
children.desc: The design system documents tokens, focus states and responsive layouts.

children.label: Decision evidence
children.desc: The decision explorer cites premises, derivations and certificates. Why-not runs on demand.

children.label: Markets app
children.desc: The markets app shows assets, charts and strategies. It never submits orders.

children.label: Identity screens
children.desc: Identity screens cover sign-in, MFA enrollment, elevation and admin tabs.

children.label: Agent dashboards
children.desc: People and agents build dashboards of query panels. Agents edit them through WebMCP tools, and every edit is visible and undoable.

children.label: Agent Terminal UI
children.desc: The terminal UI runs chat and coding sessions for developers. It sends typed commands to Arbora and streams run events back. Each effect waits for the approval of the user.

children.label: Source quality and repo standards
children.desc: The repository meets shared quality checks, docs layout and release rules.

children.label: Operation client
children.desc: The client issues typed commands. It holds pending approvals until the user decides.
children.kw: operation client|typed command|pending approval|client|failure semantics|served read|current-plan

children.label: Chat transport
children.desc: Chat runs over the served Arbora transport. Turns render live.

children.label: Native presentation
children.desc: A native front end gives full presentation parity. It reads task snapshots.

children.label: Coding session
children.desc: A coding session works in the local workspace under a workspace policy.

children.label: Tasks and runs
children.desc: One-shot tasks and background runs report into a run inspector. The harness view is read-only.

children.label: Screens and widgets
children.desc: Screens and widgets render the terminal views. Theme tokens set colors and contrast.

children.label: Geniusbot
children.desc: The desktop cockpit gives a local window onto the ecosystem. It sends operations to Arbora and shows the results. It reaches data only through Arbora.

children.label: Messaging
children.role: chat + voice channels, hosted by Arbora
children.desc: Messaging connects chat and voice channels to the system. Inbound messages go to the Arbora door, and replies go back to the channel. A supervisor starts, checks and drains each channel.

children.label: Channel supervision
children.desc: A typed state machine supervises each channel. Start waits for health. Stop drains in-flight work.

children.label: Channel adapters
children.desc: Each adapter connects one chat or push channel. Its health reflects its configuration.

children.label: Served channel gateway
children.desc: The gateway routes messages between channels and the planner.

children.label: Alerts and notifications
children.desc: Alert intake turns alerts into messages. Action notifications and webhooks dispatch from here.

children.label: Governed send
children.desc: Outbound messages pass a governed send check.

children.label: Arbora
children.role: governed runtime gateway and composition host
children.desc: Arbora is the one door to the system. It authenticates each caller, admits each request and serves operations over MCP, REST and A2A. No request reaches the engine or a connector without admission and audit.

children.label: Door: identity and admission
children.desc: The door authenticates each caller. It narrows scopes and admits or refuses each request. No request reaches the engine without passing the door.

children.label: Sign-in and federation
children.desc: Sign-in accepts federated identity providers and directory binds. It checks assertion conditions.

children.label: Local accounts and MFA
children.desc: Local accounts support optional multi-factor sign-in and recovery codes.
children.kw: mfa|totp|webauthn|recovery code|local account|api key|password|credentials for mcp

children.label: Provisioning
children.desc: A provisioning server creates and updates users from an external directory.

children.label: Elevation and scopes
children.desc: Elevation grants a temporary scope after approval. Scope intersection and revocation limit it.

children.label: Request admission
children.desc: Admission evaluates policy before dispatch. It fails closed. It screens prompts and redacts logs.

children.label: Identity ports
children.desc: Identity wiring depends only on identity ports.

children.label: Admin console and mail
children.desc: The admin console manages users and roles. A mail capability sends identity messages.

children.label: Public ingress
children.desc: The public ingress profile names the external host and identity cutover.

children.label: Served operations API
children.desc: Arbora serves every operation from one registry. One invoke pipeline applies authority, effect checks and audit. Generated HTTP and client artifacts follow the registry.

children.label: Operation registry
children.desc: The registry is immutable. It has a digest and an authorization entry for each operation.

children.label: Generated HTTP API
children.desc: Arbora generates the HTTP API, the OpenAPI document and client artifacts from the registry.
children.kw: http api|openapi|generated|swagger|client artifact|drift gate|documentation|route parity|artifacts routes|api surface|compatibility drift

children.label: Invoke pipeline
children.desc: One pipeline invokes every operation. It reserves an audit entry before a governed effect. It returns one response envelope with a closed error set.

children.label: Operation domains
children.desc: Each domain module adds a group of served operations.

children.label: Memory operations
children.desc: This module serves the memory operations.

children.label: Query and retrieval operations
children.desc: This module serves the query and retrieval operations.

children.label: Decision operations
children.desc: This module serves the decision operations.

children.label: Policy and security operations
children.desc: This module serves the policy and security operations.

children.label: Harness and evolution operations
children.desc: This module serves the harness and evolution operations.

children.label: Source operations
children.desc: This module serves the source operations.

children.label: Work and run operations
children.desc: This module serves the work and run operations.

children.label: Agent and fleet operations
children.desc: This module serves the agent and fleet operations.

children.label: Ingest and federation operations
children.desc: This module serves the ingest and federation operations.

children.label: Telemetry and usage operations
children.desc: This module serves the telemetry and usage operations.

children.label: Identity and capacity operations
children.desc: This module serves the identity and capacity operations.

children.label: Research operations
children.desc: This module serves the research operations.

children.label: Write-back operations
children.desc: This module serves the write-back operations.

children.label: Finance and markets operations
children.desc: This domain serves finance and markets operations. Market reads run server-side under the finance scope, and position and paper-trading actions check caller and subject ownership.

children.label: MCP server and multiplexer
children.desc: Arbora serves a small set of intent tools over MCP. The multiplexer finds, loads and calls fleet tools on demand. A receipt gate guards resource publication.

children.label: Multiplexer
children.desc: The multiplexer exposes four resident tools over one catalog. It loads fleet tools per session.

children.label: Intent tool surface
children.desc: The server registers the Arbora intent tools. These tools are the only MCP surface.
children.kw: intent tool|intent surface|six verbs|six resident|eight-tool|mcp projection|mcp verbs|bridge|fastmcp

children.label: Served engine backing
children.desc: Backing modules call the engine for each served tool. They record an effect journal.

children.label: Resource publication gate
children.desc: Publication refuses a resource without a valid reconciliation receipt. Only the engine issues receipts.

children.label: Retired-action runtime
children.desc: The runtime maps retired actions onto current operations.

children.label: A2A serving
children.desc: Arbora serves the agent-to-agent protocol. It admits each caller. It routes tasks and keeps conversations.

children.label: Agent cards
children.desc: A typed agent card advertises capabilities. Arbora advertises only landed capabilities.

children.label: Admission and authority
children.desc: Admission verifies the caller and the signed envelope. It fails closed when an upstream is unavailable.

children.label: Task routing
children.desc: Routing selects a target from the model profile and task class. Priority comes from the principal class.

children.label: Tasks and approvals
children.desc: Tool tasks run under a subset of allowed tools. A signed human approval chain can pause a task.

children.label: Conversations
children.desc: The served agent keeps caller conversations. It accepts binary input for the selected model.

children.label: ACP gateway
children.desc: The gateway admits conversational sessions under a typed session policy. It fails closed.

children.label: Fleet catalog and tools
children.desc: The fleet catalog admits connector servers and their packs. It onboards and renews each server. It narrows authority at discover, load and call.

children.label: Catalog and pack publisher
children.desc: A typed pack publisher builds catalog entries. Annotations carry capability, digest, cost and latency.

children.label: Onboarding and registration
children.desc: Arbora onboards each configured server. It renews every registration before the lease ends.

children.label: Skills and workflows
children.desc: Skills from installed packages join the find and load path. Arbora admits skills before they run.

children.label: Authority narrowing
children.desc: Capability checks need exact scopes. Policy narrows authority. It never widens it.

children.label: Feed events
children.desc: Typed feed events from monitoring, security audit and delivery join the catalog.

children.label: Adaptive capacity
children.desc: Capacity control throttles on the error budget. It narrows automatically and widens only by approval. Scale intents reconcile idempotently.

children.label: Per-job tool loads
children.desc: Tools load per job from the engine answer.

children.label: Write-back and repository effects
children.desc: Write-back runs only as a typed, previewed operation. Repository effects use a full request binding.

children.label: Engine binding generator
children.desc: A generator binds engine methods directly to operations. Reviewed exclusions list the gaps.

children.label: Virtual-graph sources
children.desc: Queries over connector data reach approved sources at query time. arbora runs each source read through governed fleet calls and reports the sources used.

children.label: Host composition
children.desc: Arbora composes the hosted processes. It hosts the agent server and the web UI. It imports the agent runtime only through its public interface.

children.label: Agent runtime fence
children.desc: Arbora calls the agent runtime only through public modules. The old runtime serving stack is removed.

children.label: Web UI host
children.desc: Arbora hosts the web UI. It serves the dashboard surface that the UI uses.

children.label: Browser and desktop control
children.desc: Browser and desktop actions run bound to one tenant and one run.

children.label: Serving start
children.desc: Serving start installs the decide consumers. It binds the assembler and the task planner.

children.label: Agent host
children.desc: The agent host serves the agent HTTP server and the A2A endpoints. It persists A2A tasks.

children.label: Code navigation operations
children.desc: Arbora adds operations for code navigation, index rebuilds and observation.

children.label: Unique records
children.desc: Unique records are created once. They are not upserted.

children.label: Profiles and workspace logs
children.desc: The tiny profile serves the graph with no containers. Workspace logs project per scope.

children.label: Control plane
children.desc: The control plane tracks runs, projections, sources and economics for hosted agents.

children.label: Runs
children.desc: This module holds the control-plane runs logic.

children.label: Retrieval
children.desc: This module holds the control-plane retrieval logic.

children.label: Agents
children.desc: This module holds the control-plane agents logic.

children.label: Fleet watch
children.desc: This module holds the control-plane fleet watch logic.

children.label: Webui
children.desc: This module holds the control-plane webui logic.

children.label: Migrations
children.desc: This module holds the control-plane migrations logic.

children.label: Foundation
children.desc: This module holds the control-plane foundation logic.

children.label: Gateway and widgets
children.desc: The gateway serves dashboard widgets and graph views. Widget fetches run under a bound service actor.

children.label: Connector ingest
children.desc: Arbora serves connector sources through the composed connector sync runner.

children.label: Finance and market projections
children.desc: Arbora serves finance reads, scheduled jobs and paper orders. Alerts deliver once.

children.label: Deployment and release
children.desc: Arbora deploys itself from declared profiles. It plans, applies and checks drift. It promotes releases in dependency order.

children.label: Portable deployment
children.desc: Deployment profiles cover development and production. The doctor checks served engine families.

children.label: Deployment policy as code
children.desc: A declarative manifest drives plan preview and idempotent apply. Destructive changes need approval.

children.label: Dependency-ordered release
children.desc: Releases promote in dependency order with verified digests. An exit-criteria matrix maps readiness to tests.

children.label: Acceptance evidence
children.desc: A typed checker finds acceptance-evidence gaps. Only the checker issues an accepted report.

children.label: Observability
children.desc: Arbora exports its own metrics and logs.

children.label: Agent Utilities
children.desc: Agent Utilities runs the in-run harness for each agent run. It receives a run plan from Arbora and sends facts, trace events and decision requests to the engine. It holds no store and serves no API.

children.label: Run loop and harness
children.desc: The harness applies the received run plan. It runs quality gates and constraint checks on each edit.

children.label: Harness evolution cycle
children.desc: The cycle improves the harness in five stages. The engine stores every result.

children.label: Propose
children.desc: The cycle proposes edits to harness components.

children.label: Probe
children.desc: The cycle runs probe rollouts for each proposal.

children.label: Compose
children.desc: The cycle composes the best edits into one candidate.

children.label: Persist
children.desc: The cycle writes the candidate and its receipts to the engine.

children.label: Reflect
children.desc: The cycle records lessons in the improvement library.

children.label: Cycle contract
children.desc: The cycle contract fixes the model, refusals, wiring and hot-path proof.

children.label: Plan runtime
children.desc: The plan runtime applies the run plan and its harness settings.

children.label: Gates and constraints
children.desc: Quality gates, a constraint engine and a contract validator check each edit.

children.label: Graph executor
children.desc: The graph executor builds and runs the agent step graph.

children.label: Workspace runtime
children.desc: The runtime gives local, container, browser and computer-use workspaces. It emits events and provenance.

children.label: Recursive model runner
children.desc: The recursive runner splits large inputs into recursive model calls.

children.label: Changeset development loop
children.desc: The development loop works on engine changesets, not on local trees.

children.label: Boundary deconstruction
children.desc: This program moves code out of Agent Utilities. Each package has one recorded owner.

children.label: Run loop stays
children.desc: The run loop stays in Agent Utilities.
children.kw: run loop stays|stays in agent utilities|one run|render receipt

children.label: Disposition census
children.desc: A census records one owner for each package and file.

children.label: Agent Connector SDK
children.desc: The connector SDK gives every connector one contract, one transport set and one engine adapter. It receives records from connectors and sends typed SourceIngest batches to the engine. Write-back goes only through governed approval.

children.label: Connector control
children.desc: Connector control defines the contracts that every connector follows. It certifies tools and packs.

children.label: Pack authoring and certification

children.label: Payments

children.label: Extras and optional dependencies

children.label: Source ingest

children.label: Media enrichment

children.label: Harness-session sync

children.label: Governed write-back
children.desc: Write-back routes every source change through governed authorization. It needs approval, idempotency and an audit reservation.

children.label: Repository effects
children.desc: A repository effect binds the full change. It reads back the revision after the mutation.

children.label: Approval and audit
children.desc: Approval, deterministic replay and an audit reservation protect each write.

children.label: Write-back sinks
children.desc: Sinks apply approved changes. A port composes a durable graph adapter.

children.label: Repository transport
children.desc: The repository transport hydrates code and specifications from version control. It submits bounded index batches.

children.label: Source client and workspace
children.desc: A source client reads engine changesets. A virtual workspace mount exposes them as files.

children.label: Source client
children.desc: The source client reads and writes engine changesets.

children.label: Virtual workspace mount
children.desc: The mount exposes a changeset tree as a local workspace.

children.label: Finance sources
children.desc: Finance adapters read market data, accounts and macro panels.

children.label: Observability feeds
children.desc: Monitoring, security-audit and delivery events join the durable source pipeline.

children.label: Quality and release
children.desc: The SDK builds against published engine wheels. Scanners check public documentation.

children.label: Epistemic Graph
children.role: durable multimodal knowledge, evidence, provenance, and reasoning engine
children.desc: Epistemic Graph is the store of record and the reasoning engine. It receives source batches, mutations and questions, and it returns facts, evidence and typed decisions. Every answer carries provenance, and every decision can be replayed.

children.label: Decision engine
children.desc: The decision engine answers typed questions. It applies policy and hard constraints first. It then uses entailment, exact solving and fitted statistics. It abstains when it cannot prove an answer. Every answer records an evidence class.

children.label: Decision ladder
children.desc: The ladder selects a resolution kind for each answer. It records premises and derivations. It explains why it chose an option and why it excluded the others.

children.label: Exact solver
children.desc: The solver lowers composition requirements into a bounded 0-1 integer program. It solves the program exactly. It writes a certificate that a separate verifier checks. A node budget bounds the search.

children.label: Statistical heads
children.desc: Small fitted heads rank legal options only. Calibration and conformal bounds limit their error. A head never widens the legal set. Drift makes the head abstain.

children.label: Off-policy evaluation
children.desc: Evaluation records exact propensities. It computes off-policy estimates and effective sample size. It blocks promotion when support is too low. An audit sample marks acted decisions.
children.kw: off-policy|propensit|importance sampl|effective sample|audit sampl|decisioneval|bandit|full-label|gold-label|explor|outcome aggregate|outcome link|independent outcomes|retrieval outcomes|outcome evidence

children.label: Fit jobs and head promotion

children.label: Commit and replay
children.desc: Commit re-derives the result and verifies its certificate in one transaction. A committed record replays to identical digests on every supported target.

children.label: Natural-language templates
children.desc: A natural-language request maps to a typed template. Lexical, embedding or ontology similarity selects the template. No generative model runs in this path.

children.label: Self-evolution
children.desc: This part improves the agent harness from evidence. It versions harness components and programs. It evaluates candidates against held-out tasks. It promotes a candidate only through a gated commit. Rollback re-promotes the parent revision.

children.label: Program and prompt optimizer
children.desc: The declarative program optimizer compiles signatures into programs. It searches prompts and examples with a set of optimizer kinds. It writes each result as a new program revision.

children.label: Signatures and corpora
children.desc: A signature declares typed inputs and outputs. A training corpus holds examples with splits, scores and trace references.

children.label: Optimizer kinds
children.desc: The optimizer module defines the optimizer kinds. Kinds include few-shot, bootstrap, random search, instruction search and Pareto reflection. The native compiler runs them and can stop on cancel.

children.label: Program promotion
children.desc: A promotion commit moves the champion pointer to a new revision. A compare-and-set protects it. Each revision keeps its parent reference for rollback.

children.label: ProgramOptimize job
children.desc: The engine runs program optimization as an analytics job. The job executor calls the compiler and stores the result.

children.label: Policy evolution
children.desc: Policy evolution captures traces, runs training and evaluates on held-out data. Each step writes a receipt.

children.label: Harness configuration choice
children.desc: The decision ladder chooses the harness configuration for a run. Measured signals select modes such as recursive mode.

children.label: Promotion and rollback
children.desc: A promotion gate compares paired before and after receipts. A round verdict accepts or refuses the candidate. Rollback re-promotes the parent revision through the same gate.

children.label: SourceIngest admission
children.desc: The engine admits each source batch under an accepted ingest contract. It protects replay with nonces. It re-admits stranded intents in reconcile mode.

children.label: Repository index

children.label: Ingest worker
children.desc: The engine queue serves ingest work. The connector runner executes it. Workers renew leases on long jobs.

children.label: Worker queue and leases
children.desc: Workers claim jobs from the engine queue. They renew leases and report results. The engine grants admission and scheduler floors.

children.label: Ontology induction
children.desc: Induction proposes ontology terms from text. A proposal stays a draft until it passes checks.

children.label: Fact and claim extraction
children.desc: Extraction finds facts and claims in text. It grounds them to the ontology. It repairs relation direction before commit.

children.label: Readers and knowledge atoms
children.desc: Readers turn each modality into typed fragments with span provenance. Documents become knowledge atoms.

children.label: Record materialization
children.desc: One path writes every connector record with provenance. It filters by hash and finds near-duplicates.

children.label: Source sync and reconciliation

children.kw: permission|group sync|deletion reconcil|container hierarch|content versions chain|per stream

children.label: Enrichment
children.desc: Enrichment adds derived records after admission. It fetches and enriches web documents.

children.label: Document processing
children.desc: Document processing splits documents into chunks and section trees. It keeps a processed-document record.

children.label: Media modalities
children.desc: Media modules decode audio, images and video. Speech recognition and synthesis run as engine modules.

children.label: Paper intake
children.desc: Paper intake measures the daily paper target. It admits bounded maintenance work.

children.label: External ingest adapters
children.desc: Adapters ingest external graphs, event streams and package metadata.

children.label: Source authority and changesets
children.desc: This part decides which source is the authority for each concept. It stores source code as changesets inside the graph. It also branches and merges graph state.

children.label: Source authority
children.desc: Authority rows in the ontology name the authoritative source for a concept. Selection reads these rows. Tie-break rules and ordered fallbacks record each deciding step.

children.label: Source changesets (EG-SCM)
children.desc: The engine stores source code as content-addressed blobs and changeset records. Queries materialize trees. Gate verdicts and run provenance attach to changesets.

children.label: Content-addressed blob store
children.desc: The blob store keeps file content by digest. Equal content is stored once.

children.label: Changeset records
children.desc: A changeset record names its parent and its file changes. The engine accepts changesets without a global lock.

children.label: Tree materialization
children.desc: A query materializes the file tree at any changeset. Derived indexes answer history questions.

children.label: Live code graph
children.desc: The code graph updates with each accepted changeset.

children.label: Path-scoped access
children.desc: Access control applies per path. A principal sees only the paths it may read.

children.label: Gate verdicts, bisect, revert
children.desc: Gate verdicts are graph records. The engine decides bisect and revert steps from these records.

children.label: Import and export
children.desc: Import and export keep full fidelity with external version-control history.

children.label: Simulation and agent principals
children.desc: A simulation harness exercises many agents at once. Agent-only principals carry run provenance.

children.label: Branches and merges
children.desc: Branches scope mutations. A merge runs a three-way merge per entity. It publishes the result atomically.

children.label: Query and reasoning
children.desc: The query layer plans and runs graph, relational, vector and text queries. It federates foreign sources. It reasons over the ontology with bounded steps.

children.label: UQL and planner
children.desc: The planner turns UQL into a plan. It pushes predicates down to sources. A cost model orders the steps.

children.label: Natural-language query
children.desc: A natural-language question becomes typed UQL. The engine shows the UQL. It runs it read-only.

children.label: Federation
children.desc: Federation registers foreign sources. It maps them into virtual graphs. It guards outbound calls.

children.label: Reasoning
children.desc: Reasoning derives facts with bounded steps. Truth maintenance retracts facts when premises change.

children.label: Retrieval
children.desc: Retrieval combines vector, lexical and graph signals. It returns k results or a typed shortfall.

children.label: Query languages
children.desc: The engine accepts several standard query languages. Each one compiles to the same plan model.

children.label: Wire protocol listeners
children.desc: Standard clients reach the one store through wire protocols. Each listener admits its caller through the same authenticated path as the served methods and serves catalog views that outside tools read at connect.
children.kw: wire protocol|protocol listener|postgresql wire|one store behind|wire authentication|catalog views|sql dialect

children.label: Link prediction
children.desc: Link prediction proposes new edges. It records them as hypotheses, not as facts.

children.label: Shape validation
children.desc: Shape validation checks graph data against declared shapes.

children.label: Viewport queries
children.desc: Viewport queries return bins and tiles for large views.

children.label: Table projections

children.label: Series derivations
children.desc: Series derivations compute signal states, rolling windows and barrier times with one shared distribution.

children.label: Graph compute
children.desc: Graph compute runs algorithms and numeric kernels inside the engine. Results return as typed compute results.

children.label: Graph algorithms
children.desc: The algorithm library includes centrality, paths, components, similarity and communities.

children.label: Leiden clustering
children.desc: The Leiden driver partitions a graph into well-connected communities. It runs local moving, refinement and aggregation. Ingest uses it for module detection. No hybrid partitioner runs.

children.label: Impact analysis
children.desc: Impact analysis walks dependents of a changed node.

children.label: Mining kernels
children.desc: Mining kernels find frequent sequences, process models and root causes.

children.label: Graph learning
children.desc: Graph learning trains node and edge models inside the engine.

children.label: Data science
children.desc: Data-science kernels run analytics over graph and table data.

children.label: Numeric kernels
children.desc: The numeric crate holds statistics, linear algebra and series kernels.

children.label: Quantum workloads
children.desc: Quantum modules simulate circuits and schedule hardware jobs.

children.label: Tensor and stream compute
children.desc: Tensor and stream modules compute over arrays and live event streams.

children.label: Mirror sinks

children.label: Jobs and executors

children.label: Statecharts

children.kw: redb|hot.store|write coalesc|direct state|physical layout|store authority|store files|parallel writers

children.label: Analytic lake (DataFusion)
children.desc: The lake stores columnar tables and snapshots. A vectorized query engine reads them. Acceleration policy decides what to materialize.

children.label: Time-series store
children.desc: The time-series store keeps metric samples. It answers range scans.

children.label: Vector index
children.desc: The vector index finds nearest neighbours for embeddings. Managed indexes rebuild in place.

children.label: Key-value and caches
children.desc: A key-value surface serves small records. Caches hold query results and model state.

children.label: Object storage backend
children.desc: An object-store backend keeps data on shared object storage. It commits before it acknowledges.

children.label: Graph core and indexes
children.desc: The graph core holds in-memory graph structures, indexes and cold-tier eviction.

children.label: Hybrid storage router
children.desc: The router sends each plan to the storage engine that owns its capability partition. One catalog owns placement and schema changes. Fence records keep the engines consistent.

children.label: Unified data plane
children.desc: The data plane attaches external databases as governed sources. It captures their changes. It proves conformance against each native system.

children.label: Attached-source adapters
children.desc: Adapters attach relational and document databases. Each catalog states its capture capability.

children.label: Change capture
children.desc: Change capture normalizes source changes into a durable, replayable stream.

children.label: Backup and restore
children.desc: Restore drills recover data to a point in time. They verify that the restored data matches.

children.label: Consolidation safety
children.desc: Safety rules protect attached applications that share one database.

children.label: Architecture decisions
children.desc: Architecture decisions record attached-source and hosting choices. Reviews map requests to approved decisions.

children.label: Run and conversation sources
children.desc: The data plane serves conversation history, run audit rows and step stores.

children.label: Conformance
children.desc: Conformance entries compare engine results with each native system.

children.label: Data quality
children.desc: The data plane evaluates declared quality rules over datasets and graphs. It records a score per dimension, accepts scores from outside checkers and opens a quality incident on a breach.

children.label: Virtual graphs and routing
children.desc: Approved relational mappings compile into virtual graphs. Queries push down to source SQL. A router picks native, live or accelerated paths by freshness.
children.kw: r2rml|virtual-graph|virtual graph|push down|freshness|external graph connections|schema profiles|tabular read

children.label: Ingest pipeline across stores
children.desc: A phase-ordered pipeline ingests, updates and deletes documents across every store.

children.label: Governed actions and lineage
children.desc: Governed actions have typed parameters, criteria and effects. ETL runs record lineage.

children.label: Identity and scope
children.desc: The engine checks the identity and scope of each caller. It enforces tenant sharing and secured reads.

children.label: Issuer trust
children.desc: A trust list names accepted token issuers. Each issuer has kind limits. The identity mode is a durable singleton.

children.label: Scopes
children.desc: The engine contract registers scopes. A pure subset check refuses a scope above policy.

children.label: Tenant segments
children.desc: Principal-scoped segments hold knowledge. Explicit sharing and parent chains control access.
children.kw: segment|tenant|sharing|parent chain|secured read|masking|row filter|row security|row-level security

children.label: Ownership inference
children.desc: The engine infers graph ownership from signals. It applies ownership as reversible grants.

children.label: Placement and workers
children.desc: The engine decides where deployments and workers run. Workers ask the engine and obey its grant.

children.label: Deployment placement
children.desc: A target registry lists placement targets. A pure feasibility function filters them. Why-not explains each rejected target.

children.label: Worker policy
children.desc: One engine function grants worker policy. Duplicate policy in other places is removed.

children.label: Scheduling and capacity
children.desc: Scheduling paces admission by priority class. It controls model capacity and leader election.

children.label: Finance primitives
children.desc: Finance primitives give shared numeric kernels, typed finance records and backtest provenance.

children.label: Backtest provenance
children.desc: A backtest run records mandatory provenance. Its digest matches across hosts.

children.label: Shared numeric kernels
children.desc: Shared kernels compute series statistics, risk, regimes and execution schedules.

children.label: Finance records
children.desc: Typed finance records cover accounts, lots, positions and strategies. Alerts publish through the finance outbox.

children.label: Client and contract
children.desc: The public package holds the typed client and the method contract. Quality gates protect the contract. The wheel holds no server executable.

children.label: Typed client models
children.desc: The client uses strict typed models for every method. Generated objects refuse coerced input.

children.label: Method codec
children.desc: A deterministic codec encodes method calls. A size budget limits the codec artifact.

children.label: Contract gates
children.desc: Gates check parity, dispatch reachability and scanner results. They run without bypass flags.

children.label: Distribution
children.desc: The wheel ships the contract and extension modules only. Each platform publishes on its own.

children.label: Epistemic Graph Server
children.role: package epistemic-graph-server: the one native server executable
children.desc: The server package runs the engine as one native executable. It receives network calls over standard wire protocols and passes them to the engine. Its version always matches the client package.

children.label: Executable and subcommands
children.desc: The executable starts the server and its offline subcommands.

children.label: Request dispatch
children.desc: Dispatch routes each method call to its handler. It applies request scope and cancellation.

children.label: Wire protocol adapters
children.desc: Wire adapters speak standard database and messaging protocols. Each adapter maps calls into engine methods.

children.label: Replication
children.desc: Replication keeps replicas in step through a consensus log.

children.label: Telemetry and audit
children.desc: The server exports metrics and traces. It writes an audit trail.

children.label: Container image
children.desc: The image build packages the executable for cluster deployment.

children.label: Delivery pipelines
children.desc: Pipelines holds the shared gates, Pages and release rules for every repository. It receives commits and pull requests, and it returns gate verdicts and published sites. A change lands only after its gates pass.

children.label: Gates and validation
children.desc: Gates run a fast set before landing and a full set after landing.

children.label: Fast and full gates
children.desc: Gates decide auto-revert or fix-forward.

children.label: Shared validation
children.desc: Shared validation runs bounded checks. Required checks fail closed.

children.label: Commit identity
children.desc: An allowlist limits commit author identities.

children.label: Ecosystem pages
children.desc: One generator builds documentation and spec-delivery pages for every repository.

children.label: Spec-delivery page
children.desc: The spec page shows the current state of each spec. It maps specs to code.
children.kw: spec-delivery|spec state|three states|drill-down|dependencies|repository switcher|spec delivery|reference callers

children.label: Documentation generator
children.desc: The generator builds layered documentation from registries.
children.kw: documentation|docs|home page|readme|guide|diagram|api contract|component package|architecture and reference|one generator

children.label: Repository validation hooks
children.desc: Pre-commit hooks validate tests, structure, packaging, skills and ontology governance.

children.label: Architecture explorer
children.desc: One generator reads the spec rows of every registered repository and places each on the deepest architecture part. A pinned layered layout engine lays out each level.

children.label: Connector spec delivery
children.desc: Every connector adopts the standard spec tree, hooks and page.

children.label: Delivery standard
children.desc: These rows set the delivery rules that every connector follows.
children.kw: generated status|test binding|lane contract|retired identit|changed prose|canonical title|requirement state|status generator|agent setup|agents\.md|agent-contract

children.label: Ordered digest release
children.desc: Pipelines publishes images in dependency order with digest pins. A missing kernel wheel fails the gate.

loop.label: Self-evolution loop: evaluate, promote, roll back
